### Item 271 (2026-09-26)

**Two of the three premises the ride owes are BRIDGES the arm can write today,
and the third is a component the splitter proves and throws away one line above
the place the arm would read it.**  Item 270 read every premise of
`preprocess_landing_on_stack` as true at every admitted input and none as
nameable inside the arm, and called the debt a coordinate.  A coordinate has a
price.  This is it, and item 268's `anchor=2` against `gate=49` does not enter:
nothing is transported.  BUILT: one library lemma, one repo script, two pinned
runtime censuses and one pinned table; one mislabel and one dangling reference
corrected in shipped instruments, and one location-parsing defect fixed in two
of them.

**§1 `h_le` is a BRIDGE, and the under-run is why.**  `WhiteRunUnderRun n
sp_mid sp_prep` is not the assertion that the landing failed to reach `n`; it
is that failure LOCATED — `j < n` spaces off a column-0 line start, then either
the run's end or a tab.  All three arms split it, refute the tab half at the
step (item 68) and spend the ride on the run-end half, where `sx = sp_prep`.
There the spaces ARE the landing, so `SIndent_col'` reads `sp_prep.col = j`,
`ScannerSurfCorr.col_eq` carries that to `s_prep.col`, and the arm's own
`IndentFloor sc n` bounds `n` by `minContentIndentOf sc = (max 0 (currentIndent
+ 1)).toNat`.  `underRunEnd_col_le_currentIndent` is those four steps.  It
transports nothing, so there is nowhere for it to ride and no ring to price.

The sentinel costs nothing either, and it costs nothing for a reason the family
confirms: a stack at its base floors the index at zero, `j < 0` is the
under-run's own refutation, and the conclusion is vacuous exactly where it would
be false.

**§2 The park's column is a bridge too, and item 270's OWED was the
instrument's answer.**  `sp_scan.col ≠ 0` is a field of every one of the three
constructors — `h_col0 : 0 < sp_scan.col` at `pendingProps` and
`pendingMapValue`, `h_col : sp_scan.col = n + 1` at `pendingBlock` — in a shape
`by assumption` cannot see, because `isDefEq` does not turn `0 < x` into
`x ≠ 0`.  Item 270 said as much in its own docstring (*a derivation is a
different bill from a binder*) and the caveat turned out to be load-bearing:
**the row was a reading of the question, not of the arm.**

**§3 What is NOT a bridge, and why it is not missing either.**  The third
premise is item 147's landed floor.  It is not in scope under any spelling, and
the reason is not that it is unproved: `preprocess_some_ssl_comments_anyCol`
proves it as the last component of its landed disjunct, behind the guard
`sp.col ≠ 0 → s_prep.inFlow = false`, and `preprocess_some_separate_at_floor`
returns `⟨sp_mid, h_ssl_col.1, h_ssl_col.2.1, h_ur, h_ltsl⟩` — dropping
`h_ssl_col.2.2` one line above the arm.  Both guards are payable at all three
arms: the first is §2's bridge, the second is item 270's `noflow_prep`, PAID.

**§4 What carrying it costs.**  `COORD-PRICE arms=pendingProps,pendingBlock,
pendingMapValue ident=diagonal le=BBB park_col_ne0=BBB floor=OOO lib=1
reach=BBB` (`scripts/coordinate_price.py`, pinned at
`ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.expectedCoordPrice`, battery stage 22b).

The arity flip — the under-run disjunct gains a component that is true
everywhere and is supplied in the splitter's own proof, so the census counts
sites that must now WRITE something rather than sites where the fact is hard —
breaks **five sites in ONE library declaration**, `accum_flow_open_depth0`.
Against item 268's `gate=49` that is the whole comparison.  **And the one is
the same fact item 270 ran into**: all three arms live inside that declaration,
which is why its table had to be taken at the ARM, and it is why a
by-declaration census of this widening cannot read three either.  A census
answering *how many declarations must change* and a census answering *how many
places must be written* are different questions here by a factor of five, and
the flip prints both.

Outside the module the flip breaks **THREE files** — and only one of them is a
consumer.  `Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlowStackFloorReal.lean` restates the
splitter's whole conclusion in an `example`, so it is a genuine destructuring
site; `HypothesisReaderCensus` and `ProducerDerivation` mention the splitter
nowhere and fail because they are environment censuses over the edited module,
which any text edit moves.  **An arity flip's tree census conflates consumers
with pins**, for the same reason item 266 recorded that such a flip counts
sites and not work: the probe reads what stops elaborating, and a pin stops
elaborating when a number changes.  So the honest bill outside the library is
one consumer and two re-pins, and `coordinate_price.py wide` prints the three
names rather than the count alone.

`reach=BBB` is the positive half: with the conjunct carried, every arm spends
it in one application — the park-column bridge for the first guard, item 270's
`noflow_prep` for the second.  So the third premise is not a proof obligation
either; it is a return value.

**§5 The two premises, read at the runtime.**  `bridgeFacts == (144, 144, 144,
144, 144)` (§11) reads `underRunEnd_col_le_currentIndent`'s two premises and
its conclusion where the proof cannot see them: preprocessing lands at the
built column at all 144, the park's index is at most the incoming top plus one

incoming floor is never the sentinel.

`bridgeControl == (96, 96, 96, 0, 90)` is the boundary control, taken one
column to the RIGHT — at the park's floor, which §4 of the same file measured

vacuous branch and the family's empty rows are the same six cells.**

**§6 A shipped instrument names the wrong arm.**  `scripts/arm_price.py`
calls the three arms `props`, `pendingBlock`, `pendingContent`.  The third is
`pendingMapValue`; `pendingContent` is a different arm of the same `cases` that
spends no ride, and §4 of the guard file had the right three names in prose
since item 264.  The table's twenty-four cells are unaffected — the labels are
printed, not measured — but a reader following the instrument to the source
would have been sent to the wrong arm.

It is caught by elaboration rather than by reading: each constructor declares a
binder the other two do not, so a probe that merely REFERS to one elaborates at
its own site and nowhere else, and the 3×3 matrix is diagonal.

**§7 The rule.**  **An instrument that asks whether a name is BOUND cannot
answer whether a datum is AVAILABLE, and the gap between the two is where a
coordinate's price actually lives.**  Item 270's table was right about what it
measured and its caveat was right about what it did not; running the second
question turned two thirds of a bill into nothing.  Reading either answer as
the other would have ordered a carrier ring — item 268 priced one at 2 and one
at 49 — for a datum with nowhere to ride.

**§8 What did not move.**  `accum_flow_open_depth0` still spends `dropClose` at

statement changed.  DROP reads `SITES 2` and the β.5 fixpoint is unmoved.  The one
addition is `underRunEnd_col_le_currentIndent`, which nothing yet consumes — it
is instantiated at all three arms by the instrument and by nothing in the
library.  The pricing rule *a definition nothing has instantiated is not yet
evidence* is answered here with an elaboration rather than a promise: the
instrument applies it at all three arms and reports `le=BBB`.

**§9 Gates and perturbations.**  The battery is 26 stages now: item 271 adds

and compares its table against the Lean pin the way stage 22a does, plus a
final rebuild because 22b's tree probe is held out of it.  Every instrument

**Four census pins moved, in three waves.**  `ProducerDerivation`
(`corrHyp` 433 → 434), `HypothesisReaderCensus` and `PremiseNecessityCensus`
(`constants` +1, `decls` +1, `READ` +2, `RELAY` +4 in both), and
`NarrowingWorthCensus` (`theorems` 5274 → 5275).  They surfaced one import
layer at a time because a module that fails builds none of its dependents, and
both batteries run before the chain was clean read `PINSMOVED 36` — item 269's
under-report, reproduced one item later for the same reason.  The lane moves
are justified binder by binder in one environment rather than by the aggregate
agreeing (`Verdict271.lean`): `PROP LANES read=2 relay=4 props=6 binders=13`.

**The tree census read zero twice before it read anything, and both zeros were
green.**  `coordinate_price.py`'s wide probe reported no consumer outside the
module — and the flip provably breaks one, because
`Tests/Guards/Proofs/FlowStackFloorReal.lean` restates the splitter's whole
conclusion in an `example` and proves it by the lemma.

The cause is that the two drivers spell a location differently, and the word
`error` does not merely move within the line — it crosses the path:

    lake env lean   L4YAML/…/StreamAccum.lean:11897:69: error: Tactic `assumption` failed
    lake build      error: Tests/…/FlowStackFloorReal.lean:121:22: Tactic `rfl` failed

A pattern written for either reads nothing under the other.  The first repair
was wrong for the same reason the bug was: it made the pattern search the line
instead of anchoring it, which still demanded `: error` after the column.  Under
that repair the probe reported three FAILED MODULES and zero error locations and
printed the empty census anyway.

What settles it is neither pattern but the assertion beside them: **a build that
failed while parsing no location is a broken pattern, not an empty census**, and
the probe now raises on it.  The format was then measured rather than read — a
deliberate `example : False := by rfl` under `lake build` prints the second line
above — and the parser is exercised against both real lines, plus an `info:`
line and a `trace:` line it must reject.  `scripts/wire_price.py` carried the
same anchored pattern in its own `--wide` mode, never run in a battery; it is
fixed with it.

This is the third instrument of this run whose failure mode was a GREEN reading
(item 270 found two), and all three have one shape: **the harness could not tell
"I checked and found nothing" from "I did not check."**

**Perturbations: 19 rows, 18 caught, 1 vacuous by design.**  Five components
of `bridgeFacts` and five of `bridgeControl` move under a one-off bump; four
model rows move when the state a reading is taken on is swapped, when the index
bound loses its `+ 1`, when the conclusion is narrowed from `≤` to `<`, or when
the control is stood one column left of the park's floor; and three rows
perturb the LEMMA rather than a census — weakening `j < n` to `j ≤ n`, moving
the line start off column 0, and removing the `unfold` that lets `omega` see
`minContentIndentOf` each break the proof, so none of the three premises is
decoration.

The one vacuous row is declared with its reason: reading the conclusion against
the LANDING's floor instead of the incoming one cannot move a count, because
item 269's `floorFacts` puts preprocessing at rest at the landing's own column
at all 144 — the swapped reading is `sp.col ≤ sp.col`.  The row above it reads
the split that does separate the two states, by turning `≤` into `<`.

The instrument is perturbed once, at its question: weakening the null from
`assumption` to one that cannot fail makes every row read `P`, the table reads
`le=PPP park_col_ne0=PPP floor=PPP` and the pin disagrees — which is what says
the `B` cells are the arm's and not the harness's.  That row costs a full run
of the script and is worth exactly one.

nameability gap.**  With item 272's ring PAID — the payment applied to the

**§2 The measurement.**  `slotRun` asks that the `[96]` run in front of the
park's cursor be absent or *offered a node slot*, and `offersNodeSlot`
([Token.lean:332](L4YAML/Token/Token.lean#L332)) is exactly the three block
indicators `:`, `?`, `-` — its own docstring says "After anything else a run at
an open level's own column has no slot, which is §9.2's dangling-node
violation."  `streamStart` and `documentStart` are therefore not offers, and a
document root is exactly where a `[96]` run can stand with nothing but the
start in front of it.  Five inputs, all **ACCEPTED** by `scanFiltered`, all
`slotRun = false`:

| input | the run stands behind | `slotRun` |
|---|---|---|
| `&x⏎[1]` | `streamStart` | **false** |
| `&x⏎[1, 2]` | `streamStart` | **false** |
| `--- &x⏎[1]` | `documentStart` | **false** |
| `---⏎&x⏎[1]` | `documentStart` | **false** |
| `---⏎&x !t⏎[1]` | `documentStart` | **false** |

The three block indicators do offer one (`k: &x [1]`, `- &x [1]`, `? &x [1]`
all hold), and a park with no run at all holds it by the left disjunct (`[1]`,
`k: [1]`).  The block-offer variants of the same under-run shape are refused —
`k:⏎  b:⏎    &x⏎  [1]` is `underIndentedFlowContent` and `k:⏎  -⏎[1]` is
`invalidBareDocument` — which is why the counterexamples had to come from the
document root.  Pinned as twelve `#guard`s in
[ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.lean](Tests/Guards/Proofs/ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun.lean)
§16, and the pins discriminate: flipping one expected value fails the build at
that line.

**§3 The acceptance is correct, so this is not a scanner bug.**  `&x⏎[1]` is a
legal document — the anchor property and the node it decorates may sit on
separate lines at block level — and PyYAML 6.0.3 loads all four shapes as `[1]`
(corroboration, not proof; the suite carries no case of this family and is
recorded as no evidence rather than as a negative).  **The scan SUCCEEDING is
itself the measurement that both of the close's verdicts are silent**: §8.1

either one would have refused the input.  The cell item 276 named — "a park
whose `[96]` run is offered no slot, at which BOTH verdicts are silent at the
close" — is not an empty cell.  It is inhabited, by input we accept and should.

### Item 280 (2026-10-18)

**Row 20 CLOSES: both readings of §7.1 land, and they are not alternatives —
the resolution reading is a COROLLARY of the declaration reading at the
document boundary.  A measured hole in §6.9.2's duplicate tolerance decided the

Gate: 1255 jobs, 0 errors, 7 warnings (one FEWER than the standing 8 — an unused simp argument the flip had introduced), four hygiene gates ok, serialization axioms 46 profiles; suiterunner 869 passed / 0 failed / 151 skipped, Lean suites 21/21 and `Verified: 4521/4521`. **§1 The decision as posed, and why "both" is the answer.**  Row 20 ended at one
decision — capstones 3.5–3.7's index — with two candidates: (a) index the
predicate on the DECLARATION set, §7.1's own reading; (b) keep the
document-level RESOLUTION reading, which is true but needs a new clique
invariant.  They are not alternatives, and the dependency runs one way: **(b)
is proved FROM (a).**  Per node only (a) is available, because an anchor occurs
at the `&` property while its entry in the resolution table stores a *value*
and so cannot exist until the node it decorates is complete.  At a document
boundary the two coincide, because every anchor the document declared has been
finalized by then.  So capstone 3.5 is now `parseNode_aliases_declared`
(unconditional, over `ps'.declaredAnchors`), 3.6 and 3.7 keep
`AllAliasesResolve doc.value doc.anchors` word for word, and the step between
them is `AllAliasesResolve.of_declared`, whose premise `AG.declsBound` pays.
`DeclarationsBound` is the document-entry condition; 3.6 takes it and 3.7
discharges it from the stream's initial state and the per-document reset, so
the stream-level capstone is still hypothesis-free.

**§2 The carrier went into `AG`, and the plumbing never noticed.**  `AG` now
carries three facts instead of one: the resolution table grows, the declaration
set grows, and **every name declared across a segment is already bound when the
segment ends**.  The third is transitive *because* of the first — a name bound
at the middle state is still bound at the end — so `AG.trans` still holds, and
**all 22 loop lemmas per twin compile UNCHANGED**: they use only `AG.refl`,
`AG.trans`, `AG.advance`, `AG.tryConsume`, `AG.withField` and the induction
hypothesis, so they are parametric in what `AG` means.  Only the eight leaves
moved.  That is the whole reason this cost a session rather than a week, and it
is worth writing down as a rule: **a relation whose consumers only compose it
can be strengthened at its leaves.**

`AG` had to stay a conjunction `def` and not become a `structure`, which was
measured rather than reasoned: as a structure, `AG.advance ps` stopped
typechecking against the states the plumbing threads, because those differ in
fields `AG` never reads (`nodePositions` under `trackPositions`, `currentPath`),
and a structure is rigid where a proposition over two projections is
definitionally transparent.  Three sites failed that way; the `def` version
fails at none.

**§3 The one segment without the new conjunct is the point of row 20.**
`parseNodeProperties` declares a name whose value cannot exist yet, so
`declsBound` is FALSE of it — stating it with `AG` would have been stating
something false.  That stage therefore concludes in `AG0` (the first two
conjuncts) and additionally reports what it declared, and `parseNode_ag_all`
re-establishes the missing half across the properties/finalization pair that
`parseNode` itself forms.  One lemma per twin carries it,
`declsBound_of_props_finalization`, and the two halves it joins are
`parseNodeProperties`' report and `applyNodeFinalization_binds`.  Neither half
has the property; their composition does.  **That is what "compositional" meant
in the decision text, and the naive `declaredAnchors ⊆ names anchors` is not,
because the intermediate state genuinely violates it.**

**§4 A measured hole: §6.9.2's tolerated duplicate made the resolution reading
FALSE, and fixing it improved the runtime.**  `validateNodeProps` tolerates a
duplicate anchor when the content is a collection start (the scanner's
retroactive insertion makes that real — suite 6BFJ).  `scanFiltered` refuses
two consecutive `&` outright (`invalidNodeProperties '&' 0 3`, measured), **but
the capstones quantify over token ARRAYS, not over scanner output**, and there
the hole is reachable: with the flip's in-loop `declareAnchor`, `&a &b [*a]`
is accepted with `a` declared and never bound, so
`AllAliasesResolve doc.value doc.anchors` is false over the capstones' own
domain.  The fix is one line of runtime and a better design than the patch
being landed: **declare AFTER the properties loop, from the computed
`props.anchor`** — the name the node's start event actually carries
(§3.2.2.2).  A superseded `&a` names no node, so it never becomes aliasable.
Measured after: `&a &b [*a]` → `undefinedAlias "a"`, `&a &b [*b]` → ok with
`anchors = #[b]`, the three legal self-reference shapes still load and the four
§7.1 refusals still refuse.  Two `#guard`s in
[AliasNodeRoute.lean](Tests/Guards/Proofs/AliasNodeRoute.lean) pin it over
hand-built tokens, because the scanner cannot reach the state they describe.
Three side benefits fell out: at most one declaration per properties stage *by
construction*, the properties loop touches the declaration register not at all
(so its ninety-line unrolled `_ag` proof keeps working), and the declaration is
one application rather than a `match`, which keeps `.ok (props, state)` the
shape every proof of that stage already reasons about.

**And the finding item 279's predecessor recorded is now pinned rather than
remembered.**  `parseStreamLoop` exists four times — load, raw, and the event
path's own copy in `Output/Events.lean` and `Output/EventsIx.lean` — and the
2026-10-02 flip patch cleared the declaration set in two of the four, which
would have let document 2 alias document 1's anchor on the event path while the
load path refused it.  All four now agree, measured
(`scratchpad/l4yaml-row20-aar/40-event-scope.log`) and pinned by four `#guard`
rows that read all four pipelines at once, because no test in this repo covers
that divergence class.

**§5 Two seventy-line inductions became one, over the reader.**
`parseDirectives` and `prepareDocumentState` had anchor-preservation proofs for
`anchors` alone.  Rather than copy ~75 lines per twin for `declaredAnchors`,
both are now stated over an arbitrary reader `f : ParseState → α` invariant

**§6 What the shape of the bill was, against what row 20 carried.**  The row's

**§7 NEXT.**  Row 20 is closed; the open chain is **R3 → R4 → Step 5 → Step 6**,

### Item 281 (2026-10-18)

**§1 What was asked, and the one sentence it rested on.**  Item 279 §4 wrote

**§2 The hole.**  `a⏎...⏎&x⏎[1]` is ACCEPTED by `scanFiltered`, its depth-0

with the suffix doubled, with a comment between, with a tag in the run, over a

**§3 Why the argument missed it, and what stops a third time.**  Item 278 §5
enumerated the non-offers from one refusal — "every other such shape is refused
as bare document content, because it is a second root node in one document".
That is true of every predecessor it had in view and it does not reach the
SUFFIX, because `...` does not continue a document, it ENDS one: what stands
after it is a fresh `[185] l-bare-document`, whose root node the run decorates
exactly as after `---`.  By item 278's OWN criterion — a token offers a slot
iff its production is followed by `s-l+block-node` — `documentEnd` was an offer

So the repair is not the one-arm extension, it is the census the enumeration
should have been.  `ScannerFlowOpenUnderRun` §17 probes ONE WITNESS PER
`YamlToken` KIND: `kindCensus == (17, 8, 8)` — seventeen witnesses, eight
reaching an accepted depth-0 open, all eight offered.  Two of the eight are
REDUCTIONS (`blockSequenceStart`/`blockMappingStart`: a collection's own start
is emitted before the indicator that opens the entry, so the predecessor a run
sees is that indicator, and the rows pin it); six of the 23 kinds cannot hold

what `prevRealIdx?` walks past, `comment` what `scanFiltered` filters,
`streamEnd` has nothing after it, and `flowEntry`/`flowSequenceStart`/
`flowMappingStart` stand only inside a collection, where the open is at depth
≥ 1); and the remaining nine are refusals, each pinned by the input that stops

hold: of 27 inputs, 21 dispatch a depth-0 open and NONE of their parks reads

**§4 What the repair costs, and the reason is the stack and not the
enumeration.**  Extending `offersNodeSlot` with `documentEnd` can only make
§8.1's floor fire MORE — `underIndentedFlowValuePos?` refuses when
`offered && the open's column stands on the indent stack` — and §9.2's reading
less.  Neither moves, and both reasons are measured rather than argued:

* §8.1 cannot fire after a suffix because **`...` UNWINDS the indent stack**.
  Traced across `k:⏎␣␣v⏎...⏎&x⏎[1]`, the stack reads `[-1, 0]` at the value and
  `[-1]` at the suffix, so no open's column (≥ 0) stands on it.  That is the

Measured: **1255 jobs, 0 errors, 7 warnings** (the standing seven, unmoved);
**zero pin moves in all seven guards that read the predicate**, which is
strictly cleaner than item 278's analogous extension, since no pinned input

**§5 The carrier question, answered — and all three candidates are REFUTED.**
With the fact standing again, item 279's question is live.  The cheapest
instrument is not a census of either candidate but a sweep of the STATES each

the one step left between it and the carrier to be a coordinate no hypothesis
records.

* **Lean v4.35.0 — LANDED 2026-10-17.**  This branch and its doc workspace are
  on `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`.  The release-line branch `v4.35.0` exists for
  consumers that pin by release: it began as `v4.34.0` + `145afc52` (the same
  bump applied to the pre-fix-a tree — 868 jobs, suite 4407/4407) and on
  2026-10-18 took this branch's tree by merge, resolved to this side and
  tree-identical to it, so a consumer pinning by release gets the module-system
  library.
  What the bump cost:
  * **One code change, and it was a dead name.**  v4.35.0 removes
    `Lean.ofReduceBool`, `Lean.ofReduceNat`, `Lean.trustCompiler` and
    `Lean.trustReducibility`.  `CapstoneAttr.lean` named the first three in
    `allowedCapstoneAxioms` and two of them again in its `native` classifier,
    and those five `Unknown constant` errors were the whole of the break.  A
    probe run under every installed toolchain from v4.31.0 through v4.35.0
    shows `native_decide` emitting ONLY a per-call-site
    `…_native.native_decide.ax_1_1`
    (`scratchpad/l4yaml-435-migration/native-axioms-by-version.log`), so the
    named-axiom signature had been dead here for four releases and the
    classifier's live signal was always `Name.isInternalDetail`.
    `#assert_capstone_axioms` reads 18 pure / 7 native over 25 capstones
    before and after, so no verdict moved.  Twenty prose sites across eleven
    files asserted the old signature and now name the real one.
  * **Seven pins moved, in two shapes, and no conclusion with them.**  Term
    size: `nodes` 96158 → 96125 on the twenty-four-declaration walk
    (`CloseStackCover`, `PuntCoverInputs`, `PaidLeafDelta`), 12307 → 12296
    (`ValueLinePacks`), and 12337 → 12326 with `liteNodes` 491982 → 491884
    while `alts` holds at 4312 (`ValueLineOrigins`).  Verdict lanes: `eta` +5,
    `READ` +5, `RELAY` −10 in BOTH `HypothesisReaderCensus` (369/1050/2120 →
    374/1055/2110) and `PremiseNecessityCensus` (369/1088/1983 →
    374/1093/1973) — one set of ten binder verdicts seen through two peels,
    not two drifts.  `verdictWith` reports `ETA` when a value's `lamDepth` is
    under its type's binder count, so five declarations elaborate eta-shorter
    and five relayed binders now appear applied.  Every NAMED roster held, in
    all seven files, and `constants` and `decls` did not move at all — unlike
    v4.34.0, whose four pins moved because one `toCtorIdx` left the module.
  * **The ten are unnamed, and that is the lesson.**  Naming them needs a
    v4.34.0 olean baseline to diff and none was kept — the `verdict.out` the
    reader census cites is a two-line dump of a single declaration.  This
    migration emits the roster that was missing,
    `scratchpad/l4yaml-435-migration/verdict-roster-435.out`: 3749 rows, one
    per binder, whose lane counts reproduce the pin exactly.  **A tally pin
    with no roster beside it can say that it moved and not what moved.**
  * **Pins.**  `LeanCopilot`, `importGraph`, `DocGen4` at their `v4.35.0`
    tags; the doc workspace at verso's `v4.35.0` tag (`304b8561`) with

**R4 is not parallel to R3 — it is downstream of item 64**, corrected here
2026-09-04 after measuring what the tightening costs (the diagram above used to
draw R4 as its own branch, on the strength of "nothing DEFERS to
`implicitContinue`").  That remains true and is not the constraint.  The
constraint is `entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s landing split
([StreamAccum.lean:13245](L4YAML/Proofs/Production/StreamAccum.lean)), which
reads `by_cases hnw : n ≤ w` and spends `valueMapRoute hnw` over
`nestedBlockMap`.  Carrying `0 < m` turns that side condition into `n < w`, so
the EQUAL-width landing loses its route and falls to the pack's `Or.inr` —
strictly enlarging the punt R3's item 65 exists to drain.  The input is
`k:⏎  :⏎  b: 2`, and the events say what it should read as instead: the parser
emits ONE inner mapping with two entries at width 2 (`=VAL :` / `=VAL :` /
`=VAL :b` / `=VAL :2`), so the honest reading closes the awaited entry with
`e-node` and CONTINUES the same `[187]` — the sibling composition item 64's
run-end half has to build anyway.  Build it once; then R4's tightening has somewhere to send the equal-width case,
and 1c and 1d can go as one session.  Items 64 and 65 LOCATED it rather than
building it — `DedentLanding` and `KeyPackPunt.dedent` — because the reading it
needs is a frame stack on the pending, which is row 19's own item.

pack's resume twin threads it, and `entryKeyPack_of_dispatch`'s dedent
branch conses at the landing's level — the equal-width case has its
somewhere.  R4 is UNBLOCKED.

stands as written.  1d does not: the equal-width landing is only one of THREE
families that reach `m = 0`, the other two being the root's own mapping and the

**The construction, consumer-probed** (`591-keyframes-probe.lean`, zero
diagnostics):

```lean
inductive KeyFrames (P : SurfPos → Prop) : List Nat → SurfPos → Prop where
  | bottom (sp) (h_bot : P sp) : KeyFrames P [] sp
  | mapLevel (k ks sp) (h_lt : ∀ k' ∈ ks, k' < k)
      (h_cont : ∀ sp_end, SCompactMapTail k sp sp_end → KeyFrames P ks sp_end) : KeyFrames P (k :: ks) sp
  | seqLevel (k ks sp) (h_lt : ∀ k' ∈ ks, k' < k)
      (h_cont : ∀ sp_end, SCompactSeqTail k sp sp_end → KeyFrames P ks sp_end) : KeyFrames P (k :: ks) sp
```

with `KeyFrames.close` (every level's empty tail, to the bottom),
`KeyFrames.ofResumeFrames` (every mapping-lane stack embeds, so the existing
`h_closeFV`/`h_framesV` payments ride unchanged), and `KeyFrames.resumeAt`,
`ResumeFrames.resumeAt`'s proof with the two constructors' arms sharing the
`ResumeWidths` bookkeeping — the level at the landing's width hands back a
mapping tail OR a sequence tail.  On it, the three terms the construction
needs: **the spend** at `accum_block_on_closeThenBlock`'s landed-`-` arm — the
closed park's stack at the landing, `resumeAt` the landing's width `k`
(membership by the scanner's unwind, item 149's argument: a width matching no
open level is `trailingContent`, refused before dispatch), the sequence case
conses the new entry (`SCompactSeqTail.cons`) and gives the new park its own
`h_kslot` as the stack closed and its own stack as the levels above `k`, the
mapping case declining (a `-` at a mapping level's width is the value lane's
`h_mapFV`, not this spend's); **the payer** at the nested `-` — the outer
entry's sequence level pushed on the outer park's stack, the outer entry's node
being the inner collection over the same `compactSeq`/`nestedBlockSeq` crossing
the outer `h_kslot` payment writes today; **the bottom** — item 188's park, a
top-level entry of the frame's key sequence, whose stack is `[]` over its own
`h_kslot`.

`pendingBlock.h_kslot` and `pendingBlockContent.h_kslot` themselves, GENERALIZED:
`∃ nv, node → tail → ExplValueLine sp_start nv` becomes `∃ nv ks, node → tail →
KeyFrames (ExplValueLine sp_start nv) ks` — every consumer that spent the line
spends `.close` of the stack (one lemma), every payer that paid the line pays

what that `nil` discards).  This keeps the pack family at its 103 sites — a new

and its three lemmas beside `ResumeFrames`, no consumer touched; (b) the two

**Step 12.3.4.1 (a) BUILT — `KeyFrames`, the value-line resume stack over mixed
levels, with `close`, `ofResumeFrames` and a kind-aware `resumeAt`, beside
`ResumeFrames` in `StreamAccum`; nothing reads it yet.**  [Item 302](#item-302-2026-10-20)
consumer-probed the stack and priced 12.3.4.1 in three parts; this is the first:
the inductive and its three lemmas, exactly as probe 591 states them, landed in
the library (`StreamAccum.lean` +94, after `ResumeFrames.resumeAt`; the dev
patch is `scratchpad/l4yaml-row12-steps/598-dev-303.py`).  No consumer is
touched, so the library's behavior does not change; what moves is the three
censuses that count the module's declarations, and each is re-pinned with the
rows it gains named.

```lean
inductive KeyFrames (P : SurfPos → Prop) : List Nat → SurfPos → Prop where
  | bottom (sp) (h_bot : P sp) : KeyFrames P [] sp
  | mapLevel (k ks sp) (h_lt : ∀ k' ∈ ks, k' < k)
      (h_cont : ∀ sp_end, SCompactMapTail k sp sp_end → KeyFrames P ks sp_end) : KeyFrames P (k :: ks) sp
  | seqLevel (k ks sp) (h_lt : ∀ k' ∈ ks, k' < k)
      (h_cont : ∀ sp_end, SCompactSeqTail k sp sp_end → KeyFrames P ks sp_end) : KeyFrames P (k :: ks) sp
```

`KeyFrames.close` closes every level with its empty tail to the bottom;
`KeyFrames.ofResumeFrames` embeds every mapping-lane stack level for level, so
the payments `h_closeFV`/`h_framesV` carry ride unchanged into the new stack;
`KeyFrames.resumeAt` is `ResumeFrames.resumeAt`'s proof with the two
constructors' arms sharing the `ResumeWidths` bookkeeping, the level at the
landing's width handing back a mapping tail OR a sequence tail.  The docstring
carries item 167's reason for the stream's one width and why the value line
cannot have one.

**What building the mode taught about the instrument — five fixes, each from a run that lied.**
(1) Lean stops at 100 errors (`maxErrors`): every round of items 301–311's census was capped at
100 sites plus the cap notice, so the "four rounds" of item 311 measured the cap, not the
component (corrected in that entry); the census now runs `lean -DmaxErrors=5000` and skips a
cap notice should one appear.  (2) `has type`/`but is expected to have type` are not indented in
Lean's message, so the reader that kept only indented lines lost every type and classified every
state relay as a `∨ True` relay; the reader now keeps a message until the next `file:line:col:`
header.  (3) The alternative that decides a relay is the OUTERMOST `∨`'s right side — a type that
mentions an inner `… ∨ True` cover option is not a `∨ True` source.  (4) An argument identifier
followed by further arguments (`… h_expl105 h_vslot105`) is a relay when the message says
`Application type mismatch`; a keyword (`fun`, `by`, `⟨`) never is.  (5) A mismatch at one
component of a tuple leaves its siblings' expected types open, so an `omega` or an anonymous
constructor fails in the same round for no reason of its own: such a CASCADE is skipped once and
is an UNHANDLED stop only if it recurs after its cause is sorried.  Each round's raw output is
now kept beside the TSV (`…-roundN.out`), which is how (2) was found.

**What this does and does not reach.**  No library file changes and nothing is paid; the step buys the
number lane (b) is measured against and the reading that every transport is one dispatch wide.  NEXT is
lane (b), the content lane, in the order the residue names: the fourteen `accum_content_pending`
transports and the two in `content_dispatch_routed` through one preservation lemma for the content
dispatch (`ExplicitValueRefused sc → ExplicitValueRefused s'` from `preprocess_preserves_explicitKey`,
`dispatchContent_preserves_explicitKeyLine` and the indent twin), then the content lemmas' 41 declines
and `content_dispatch_routed`'s 29 — the leaves through the same lemma, the roots from `h_noek` with
`PackAlt.ofRefused` — each payment read back on this line (`relayState` 20 → …, `decline` 245 → …).
The content lane's consumer probe is the lemma applied at one site, which the residue's own round
then confirms; it is run before the lane is priced further.

roots + 1 transport, `question_open_map` 3 leaves); the FLOW lane (`accum_flow_open_depth0` 2 + 6,

are the parks' pack and stack fields (`h_kslot`, `h_kslotUp`, `h_closeFV_old`, `h_expl51`, `h_explUp190`,
`h_vslot`, `h_resSeqV`, `hkv`, …) and the resume continuations (`cont`, `contv`), the roots the new
fields of the parks the step builds.

**Lane (c), the block lane — one invariant, then one lemma per indicator.**  The block step is the
preprocess followed by `-` (`scanBlockEntry`), `:` (`scanValue`) or `?` (`scanKey`).  The register:
`-` writes neither register field (`ExplicitKeyCoupling.scanBlockEntry_preserves_explicitKey`), `:` keeps
a dead register dead (`scanValue_ok_of_ekl_none`), `?` makes it LIVE (`scanKey_ok_explicitKey`).  The
indent: `-` and `?` push a level (`scanBlockEntry_indents`, `scanKey_indents`), so `currentIndent = -1`
never survives them — the predicate's second disjunct cannot transport across a `-` or `:`.  What does
transport is the first disjunct alone, and a park's alternative IS its first disjunct under one fact:
**a live register stands on a pushed indent** — `currentIndent = -1 → explicitKeyLine = none` — which
holds at every park but a marker's, because `scanKey` pushes the indent it records and only
`scanDocumentStart`/`scanDocumentEnd` empty the stack (`unwindIndents` cannot pop below a column ≥ 0).
With it, `-` and `:` transport in one line each; without it they do not transport at all.  The two
lemmas, stated with the invariant as a premise and checked against the built library
(`863-probe-316.lean`, `863-probe-316.out`): the probe's three theorems — `step_blockEntry` and `step_value` with `h_inv : NotMarker sc`, and `no_step_key : s'.explicitKeyLine ≠ none`
after `scanKey` — elaborate with no diagnostics against the built tree (`863-probe-316.out` is empty); two slips on the way, a
`simpa` that cannot see `peek?` through a structure update (`exact` can) and `Option.noConfusion` where `Option.some_ne_none` is
the lemma, are in the log.  The price of lane (c) is therefore the
invariant as a `PendingNode` fact — derivable at `noPending` (`h_noek` gives the register dead
outright), vacuous at the parks that carry a pushed indent (`pendingMapValue`'s `h_park_top`,
`pendingBlock`'s floor), to be carried by the others — and its producers; then 70 leaves and 3
transports pay mechanically, the way items 313–315 paid the content lane.

**Lane (f), the `?` lane — payments, not transports.**  `question_open_map`'s three leaves and the
key-pack lemmas' twelve resumed sequence levels are not relays of an alternative: after `?` the
register is live and the indent pushed (`no_step_key` in the probe), so `PackAlt s'` is FALSE at the
park the step builds and no `Or.inr` can stand there.  The frame's own value line is what the `?`
opened (`frameChainOne` on the new frame); the declining arm — the enclosing chain declined — must build
the stack from the new frame alone.  These are the "face roots" of item 308, re-read: real stack
payments at nine sites.

**Lane (e), the marker lane.**  `pendingDocStart`/`pendingDocEnd` carry `h_docline`, `h_marker_tail`,
`h_nic`, `h_arm`, `h_nodir` — no indent fact.  Item 308's price stands: a `currentIndent = -1` fact
on both parks (three producers), from which `PackAlt.ofRefused (Or.inr …)` pays the four marker roots.
What this item adds: a `-` after a marker converts a `-1` park into a `0`-indent park with the register
possibly LIVE (a `?` frame crossing `---`, probe 726), so the invariant fails there by construction and
the `-`-after-marker arm must pay a real pack or be refuted — the first place the completeness proof
will say whether the scanner over-accepts `? a⏎---⏎- b⏎: v` (CLAUDE.md §10: a latent bug is an
unprovable obligation; the input goes through both pipelines and libyaml before anything is proved).

**Lane (d), the flow lane.**  `PackAltG g` is a placeholder (item 311): the frame's alternative needs the
open-time state or the register pair the open pushes on `explicitKeyStack`, carried to the close;
`accum_flow_open_depth0`'s eight sites, `accum_step_flow`'s two and `compact_open_map`'s standing transport

**Lane (g), `pendingFlow`.**  Unchanged: goes with 12.4.

**What this does and does not reach.**  No site is paid; the residue stands at
`decline=178 relayState=3`.  What the item buys is the ORDER: the invariant first (item 317), since

### Item 317 (2026-10-21)

**A scanner over-acceptance found by the proof, fixed in both pipelines: a document marker now
ends the explicit-key register.**  Item 316 priced the block lane's transports and found every one
waiting on the invariant *a live register stands on a pushed indent*, true everywhere but at a
marker — because the register SURVIVED `---`/`...` (item 308's probe 726).  Before building that
invariant, this item asked whether the survival is a fact or a bug (CLAUDE.md §10: build the input
the branch describes and run it).  It is a bug.

**The diagnosis** (`864-marker-inputs/`, `864-marker-pipelines-full.out`, `864-marker-tryscan.out`;
PyYAML 6.0.3 with libyaml as the reference):

| input | libyaml | L4YAML before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `? a⏎---⏎- b⏎: v` | refused (block collection) | **accepted**: `… +DOC --- +SEQ =VAL :b -SEQ -DOC +DOC =VAL : -DOC` — a third document, an empty scalar, out of a `:` the stale `? a` register read as the explicit value of a key in the PREVIOUS document | refused, `trailing content at line 3, column 0` |
| `- b⏎: v` (control, no marker) | refused | refused, `trailing content at line 1, column 0` | unchanged |
| `? a⏎: b⏎---⏎- c⏎: v` (control, register reset by `: b`) | refused | refused, `trailing content at line 4, column 0` | unchanged |
| `? a⏎---⏎: v`, `- ? a⏎---⏎: v` | refused | refused, `value indicator ':' … expected column -1` — the stale register again, in the other direction | accepted as `… +DOC --- +MAP =VAL : =VAL :v -MAP` |
| `: v`, `---⏎: v`, `a⏎---⏎: v` (controls) | refused | accepted as an empty-key mapping | unchanged |

The control row decides it: L4YAML refuses `- b⏎: v` on its own and accepts it behind a `?` that a
marker should have closed, so the register that crossed the marker is the cause and nothing else.
The last two rows are the same fact seen from the other side — a `:` opening the next document was
refused for a key that no longer existed; after the fix the second document reads as it does without
a first one.  On the bare `: v` L4YAML and libyaml differ by design: YAML 1.2.2 example 8.18 (`: #
Both empty`) admits an implicit entry with an empty key and L4YAML implements it; libyaml does not.
The corpus has no document that
opens with `:` (`grep '^: '` over `yaml-test-suite/src` finds none), so the reading rests on the grammar: [188]
`ns-l-block-map-implicit-entry` admits `e-node` as the implicit key, and `? a⏎---⏎: v` after the fix is two
documents, `{a: ~}` and `{"": v}`, exactly as `---⏎: v` already was.

**The fix** (`Scanner/Document.lean`: `scanDocumentStart`, `scanDocumentEnd`;
`Scanner/IndexedDispatch.lean`: `scanDocumentStartIx`, `scanDocumentEndIx`): each marker's final
state update sets `explicitKeyLine := none, explicitKeyCol := -1` beside the flags it already
resets — a document marker ends every open node, the `?` frame among them.  The register's writers
are now `?`, `:`, the flow opens and closes, the flow entry, and the two markers.  Probe 726 re-run
against the fixed scanner (`866-marker-register-probe.py`, `866-marker-register-probe-after-fix.out`):
`ekl_after=none ekc_after=-1` at each of the sixteen markers in its fourteen inputs.

**Gates** (`875-gates-317.sh`, log `875-gates-317.log`, reports under `875-gates-317/`).  `run-all-tests.sh`
exit 0: seventeen suites, **2141/2141** by the suites' own `Results:` lines (the previous local report, of

PARSER — `yaml.parse`, since `safe_load` refuses every one of these at construction, a list is no dict
key — agree on all six): `?⏎- a⏎- b⏎: v`, `?⏎- a⏎  - b⏎- c⏎: v` and `? - a⏎  - b⏎: v` are accepted as `+MAP

c` are REFUSED by both — L4YAML's scanner with `invalid implicit key` or `trailing content`, PyYAML with
`mapping values are not allowed here` or `while parsing a block collection`.  So the future a
side-condition site cannot produce a fact for — a compact MAP tail at a level the stack holds as a
SEQUENCE, or at a level the stack does not hold — is one the scanner refuses when it arrives.  The proof
cannot spend that: the field quantifies over surface derivations of the tail, which exist, and promises
`KeyFrames` for a stream the grammar does not contain.  **The finding, for the plan — a decision, not a payment.**  At the twelve sites the field's `∨` offers two
things, a resume fact about a tail and a dead register, and neither holds: the register is LIVE (a `?` frame
is open, which is why the park carries these fields at all), and the fact promises `KeyFrames` for a stream
the grammar does not contain.  Three readings, each priced by what it touches.  **(A) Widen the alternative**
to what the sites actually have — `PackAlt sc := ExplicitValueRefused sc ∨ <the stack holds level k as a
sequence, or holds no level k>` — a stack-shape fact the park already carries (`h_mapFV`, `h_closeFV_old`),
which the class-A consumer (12.3.4.3) must then refute from its own reading of the same stack; price: one body
(the flip census reads it), the twelve sites pay by projection, and the refutation at the consumer gains a
case whose proof is the scanner's `invalidImplicitKey` seen from the park — a second scanner-state fact to
carry.  **(B) Make the resume facts conditional on the level's kind** — `levelIsMap k → ∀ sp_end,
SCompactMapTail k sp_mid sp_end → …` — so each side-condition branch is vacuous by its own premise and the
`∨ PackAlt` stays what it is; price: six constructor fields and their twins change type, every producer and
consumer of them is touched (the residue census can count them before they are built), no new disjunct.
**(C) Prove the fact vacuously** from a surface lemma `no compact map tail after a sequence level` —
refuted by the type itself: `SCompactMapTail k sp_mid sp_end` is a relation on positions that does not see
what precedes `sp_mid`; the refusal is the stream grammar's and the scanner's, not the tail's.  (C) is out.
Between (A) and (B), (B) says what a resume fact means (it resumes a level of one kind) and keeps the
alternative the single register fact that 12.3.4.3 refutes in one way; (A) keeps the fields and moves the
burden to the consumer.  This is NFR's call — 12.3.4.2's design, not a lane's payment — and the row carries
it as OPEN with the twelve sites named (`900-skipped-319.tsv`, the `side-condition` rows).

### Item 326 (2026-10-21)

**Step 12.3.4.2, lane (f) MEASURED — no library change.  The lemma item 323 named for `question_open_map`'s two leaves — a
dead register means no `?` frame is open above, so the chain the new park carries is empty — is FALSE, and the two leaves
join item 320's A/B class.**

**The claim** (item 323).  In `question_open_map`, `h_upAll`'s declining arm (`| Or.inr _ => Or.inr trivial`, twice) holds
the old park's dead register; item 323 read that as "no `?` frame was open above", made the honest payment
`Or.inl ⟨[], …⟩` (the empty ancestor chain), and named the lemma connecting the two as lane (f)'s content.

**The experiment** (`1020-reference.py`/`.out`; `1021-question-chain-register-probe.py`/`.out`, the scanner's register
before and after every `?` and `:` token).  `?⏎  ? y⏎  : z⏎  ? q⏎: w` is accepted by both pipelines and by libyaml as
`{{y: z, q: ~}: w}`.  At `? q` the register is dead — `: z`, the inner entry's explicit value, cleared it
(`ekl_before=some 1`, `ekl_after=none`) — while the outer `?` of line 0 is open and its value `: w` follows.  In
`?⏎  ? y⏎  : z⏎: w` the outer value is scanned with a dead register itself (`ekl_before=none` at `: w`): the register
tracks the latest explicit key, not the stack of open ones, and an outer `?`'s value is the dedent reading `h_upAll`
carries (item 197).  So a dead register at the old park does not mean an empty chain: at `? q` the new park's
`h_explUp`-class fields must carry the outer frame for `: w`, and `Or.inl ⟨[], …⟩` would be a false reading of that state.
Control: `?⏎  y: z⏎  ? q⏎: w` keeps the register live through `y: z` — an implicit key's `:` does not clear it.  All seven
inputs agree across the two pipelines; libyaml agrees on six, the exception `k:⏎  ? y⏎  : z⏎  ? q⏎: w`, which L4YAML
reads with an empty-key last entry (item 317's reading).

**What it changes.**  There is no lemma to prove for these two leaves.  `h_upAll`'s alternative, the dead register, drops
the chain the next `?` must carry, so the leaves pose the question item 320 put to NFR for the resume facts: the
alternative of a chain-carrying field becomes a stack fact (A), or its producers always carry the chain (B).  Item 323's
entry carries the correction.

**Row 12, step 4 of item 331's order — PAID, landed: the scanner keeps one pending explicit key per indentation level (`ScannerState.pendingKeys`, in lockstep with `indents`) and re-reads the register off that stack whenever a level's key closes.**  The conformance fix item 334 §3 priced: `?⏎  ? y⏎  : z⏎: w: x` and its `? q` variant are accepted (libyaml's reading); 306 frags³ acceptances the stale register was manufacturing are refused.

**The mandate.**  Item 333's NEXT:

> **NEXT — step 3 of item 331's order: the flow frame reads the pushed register pair.**  `PackAltG (e, ec) := e = none`

Item 334 (PR #34, docs-only, not yet on this branch — declared gap) found step 3 has nothing to pay before the flip, and set step 4 next: "`IndentEntry.pendingKey` in both pipelines — the conformance fix for `?⏎  ? y⏎  : z⏎: w: x` and the retirement of the `ns` chains".  This item pays the scanner half; the `ns`-chain retirement is the proof half and stays with the flip (the invariant must READ `pendingKeys` before any chain can go — Rule 8 counts the field ghost until then).

**Design (both pipelines, byte-identical shapes).**  `pendingKeys : Array (Option Nat) := #[none]`, pushed/popped wherever `indents` is (`pushMappingIndent`, `pushSequenceIndent`, `unwindIndentsLoop`, the flow push/pop paths).  `scanKey` marks the innermost level's slot in the same record write that arms the register.  `scanValue` settles `(pendingKeys, explicitKeyLine, explicitKeyCol)` through one named predicate `scanValueKeySurvives s s_kc` (flow: never; block: a dead register has nothing to close, a live one survives an implicit `:` deeper than its column) and one triple: survive → unchanged; otherwise `PendingKeys.close cols pks ekc` — close the level at the register's column, re-read the innermost pending key (`PendingKeys.innermost`, deepest `some`).  A flow `:` clears every slot.  `closeStaleExplicitKey(Ix)` (item 333) now re-reads instead of resetting, and its `:` exception is narrowed to the key's own column: a `:` strictly LEFT of a stale `?` closes it (the dedent already popped its level; the re-read hands the register to the outer `?`).  `-`/`?` keep item 333's exception wholesale (a `-` left of the key kept `- ? a⏎- : b`'s refusal pinned in `BlockDeferralClasses`).

**Why a separate array and not `IndentEntry.pendingKey`.**  The probe on `IndentEntry` touched every `{ column := _, isSequence := _ }` literal in 44 guard files (item 332's P5 lesson); a lockstep array moves only the record writes that push/pop, and the `indentColumns` projection gives the proofs the pair.  Folding it into `IndentEntry` stays open for the flip, when `Covered` becomes an equality with `sc.indents`.

**The carrier** (`ColFloor.lean` §1):

```
Forward s s' := s.line < s'.line ∨ (s'.line = s.line ∧ s.col ≤ s'.col)      -- the cursor never moves back
Behind p s   := p.line < s.line ∨ (p.line = s.line ∧ p.col ≤ s.col)

structure ColFloor (s : ScannerState) : Prop where
  floor : s.needIndentCheck = false → s.currentIndent ≤ (s.col : Int)
```

## Indexed-pipeline parity gap

**CLOSED 2026-08-06 — full parity.** Found 2026-08-05 from downstream
(`algctl` in `soil-moisture-workflows` parses its DPS configs with
`parseYamlWithCommentsIx`, and its `notes: >` blocks came back one byte short
of both PyYAML and our own legacy pipeline). This outranked the proof work
because `parseYamlWithCommentsIx` is the entry point consumers actually call —
it is the only one carrying `nodePositions`, so anything editing YAML in place
must use it — while every gate we had (matrix scores, round-trip corpus, the
proofs) ran through the **legacy** `TokenParser.parseYaml`.

The fix ran in three plan items: **P0** indexed the dead parity harness into
`Tests.Guards` and repaired its `agree` comparison (it compared `Except`s with
`==`, for which core has no `BEq`, so the file could not have compiled even if
it had been imported); **item 6** ported the seven legacy fixes the twin lagged
(B1/B2/B3/C1/C2/C3/E) and fixed what the new coverage found (D5 —
`needIndentCheck` after a block scalar; zero-indent block scalars via
`indentFloor`; the missing §6.7 header-newline guard); **item 7** transcribed
the six missing legacy strictness checks as read-only validator walkers plus
dispatcher/preprocess throws (tab-as-indentation in two contexts, §8.1.3
auto-detect validation, doc-markers + under-indent + tab in quoted
continuations, §6.6 comment-needs-whitespace, §6.7 header `#` glue).

The standing lesson is recorded in
[Proof-breaking code patterns](#proof-breaking-code-patterns): a probe that is
not indexed into a default target is not a probe. Full divergence analysis
(D1–D5), the per-item work-lists and the 35 block-scalar parity guards are in
git.

## Surrogate hex escapes decoded to NUL

**CLOSED 2026-08-11.** `\uD800`–`\uDFFF`, and the same code points written
`\U0000D800`, decoded to **U+0000** instead of being rejected — silent data
corruption on *accepted* input, in both pipelines, which survived a round-trip
as `a: "\0"` and put a raw control byte in the event stream.

The root cause was one guard. `parseHexEscape`
([Scanner/Scalar.lean:80](L4YAML/Scanner/Scalar.lean)) and `parseHexEscapeIx`
([Scanner/IndexedScanner.lean:512](L4YAML/Scanner/IndexedScanner.lean)) tested
`val < 0x110000`, which is strictly weaker than the precondition of the function
they then called: `Char.ofNat` is total —
`dite n.isValidChar (Char.ofNatAux n) (fun _ => '\0')` — and its else-branch
**substitutes** rather than fails. The two conditions disagree on exactly the
2048 surrogates, so every one of them took the *success* branch and decoded to
NUL with no diagnostic.

Both guards are now `Nat.isValidChar` itself, so the substituting branch is
unreachable from the scanners rather than merely unvisited. A lone surrogate is
not a Unicode scalar value and has no UTF-8 encoding, so it cannot be a
character of any scalar in the representation graph (§5.1); `[60]`/`[61]`
constrain the decoded value not at all, which is the spec's gap, but §5.1
settles it for a conforming processor. Measured after the fix: all five shapes
(including the UTF-16 pair `\uD83D\uDE00`) reject in both pipelines, and
U+D7FF / U+E000 / U+10FFFF / `\x41` still decode — the guard is a hole in the
code-point line, not a ceiling.

**The proof-side claim asserting this could not happen was also false**, and its
shape is the reusable part.
[Proofs/Errors/EscapeResolution.lean](L4YAML/Proofs/Errors/EscapeResolution.lean)
§4 read: "Either the decoded code point is < 0x110000, in which case
`Char.ofNat` produces a valid Unicode char by construction, or the scanner
returns `.unicodeOutOfRange`." Both halves are true and the disjunction is still
not a safety property. The citation "produces a valid Unicode char" was doing
the work of a *faithfulness* claim while asserting only *inhabitation* — and the
lemma behind it, `char_isValidChar`, quantifies over the codomain, so `'\0'`
satisfies it. The same file simultaneously documented a U+FFFD "fallback" that
no branch implements; prose asserting two incompatible fallbacks is the tell
that neither was checked. What replaces it is checkable:
`CharClass.toNat_ofNat_of_isValidChar` — under the guard, the decoded
character's code point **is** the requested value — carried by the indexed twin
as a conjunct of `parseHexEscapeIx_decoded`.

Pins: `Tests/Reflections/SurrogateEscapeRejected.lean` (five rejections and four
byte-exact boundary streams per pipeline, plus the `Char.ofNat 0xD800 =
Char.ofNat 0xDFFF` counterexample) and nine `#guard`s in
`Tests/Guards/Proofs/EscapeResolution.lean`. The principle is
**Reflection 642**.

**Cost, against the estimate.** The emitter was structurally immune as priced —
`escapeChar` emits hex only as `\xHH` for values ≤ 0x1F, so the three 2-digit
`native_decide` bounds re-proved verbatim under the stronger guard, restated
from `< 0x110000` to `Nat.isValidChar`. Four `simp only [h_val_lt, ↓reduceIte]`
lines in the two emitter-scannability files needed no change at all once their
bound lemmas were restated. Matrix unchanged on both instrument sets;
`run-all-tests.sh` 4439/4439; full build 954 targets, warning-free.

Two things the estimate got wrong, both cheaper than expected. The duplicate-key
question ("do collapsed surrogate keys make `duplicateKeyPolicy := .error` fire
spuriously?") is **moot**, not untested: the inputs that would collapse are now
rejected before a key is ever built. And the indexed twin needed no error
channel, because the divergence is not specific to this member — see the
residual item below.

**Residual, recorded not fixed:** the *whole* escape-error family is
message-diverse between the pipelines. `\q`, `\u12`, `\x4`, `\U0011` and
`\U00110000` all surface as `unterminatedDoubleQuoted` from the indexed caller
where legacy names the specific fault, because `parseHexEscapeIx` returns
`Option` and `processEscapeIx` has no `ScanError` channel at all. Verdict-equal
in every case, invisible to the matrix (no suite case carries a malformed
escape). Filed under [Other open items](#other-open-items); giving the indexed
escape path an error channel is a self-contained piece of work whose real cost
is `parseHexEscapeIx`'s `Option` being load-bearing for
`parseHexEscapeIx_offset_monotonic`.

## Grammar completeness plan

*(was `GRAMMAR_COMPLETENESS_PLAN.md`, itself formerly `VERSION-0.4.8.md`;
consolidated into this file 2026-08-01. Completed steps are recorded here as
closure records only — the blow-by-blow progress history is in git.)*

**Goal:** prove that syntactic acceptance by `parseYaml` and membership in the
YAML 1.2.2 surface language are the same predicate, and close the biconditional
that says so.

**The biconditional this plan was written around is FALSE as stated** (recorded
2026-09-28, from an independent audit of `main` at `16562a7` by Heath Sanchez of
[Metalogic Labs](https://metalogiclabs.xyz/)):

```lean
theorem parse_iff_grammar (input : String) :   -- ~~REFUTED — do not attempt~~
    (∃ docs, parseYaml input = .ok docs) ↔ InYamlLanguage input
```

- **Forward** (v0.4.6, proven): `parseYaml input = .ok docs → InYamlLanguage input`.
  This direction stands and is unaffected.
- **Converse**: `InYamlLanguage input → ∃ docs, parseYaml input = .ok docs` — **false**,
  and false for two independent reasons that price differently.

**Reason 1 — over-approximation, repairable by narrowing.** `InYamlLanguage`
derives strings the runtime rejects because a production is looser than the
spec: `scannerDrop` (row 12), `implicitContinue` (row 19), and the fifth and
sixth found by the audit, `[82] l-directive` and `[162] c-b-block-header` (see
[The over-approximation problem](#the-over-approximation-problem)).  Each is
closed by tightening the production, and that is what rows 12 and 19 do.
Measured on this branch: `%YAML .2⏎---⏎a` is derivable and
`parseYaml` answers `unexpected content after directive at line 0, column 8`.

**Reason 2 — a layer the surface language cannot address, NOT repairable by
narrowing.** `parseYaml` enforces per-document conditions that are not
syntactic, and the surface language has no vocabulary for them: every relation
in `L4YAML/Surface/` is `SurfPos → SurfPos → Prop` with **no environment
parameter anywhere**, so `InYamlLanguage` cannot STATE the condition at any
tightness.  Measured on this branch with `lake exe tryparse`:

| input | `InYamlLanguage` | `parseYaml` |
|---|---|---|
| `*x` | derivable | `undefined alias '*x' … no preceding '&x' anchor in this document (§7.1)` |
| `!h!x` | derivable | `undeclared tag handle '!h!' … use %TAG directive to declare it (§6.8.2.2)` |

No narrowing of any production removes these: the anchor that would make `*x`
legal is a fact about *what came before it in the same document*, and the
surface relations cannot see it.  This is a change of LAYER.

**The corrected target** (chosen 2026-09-27 from the two shapes the audit
proposed; this is its "option 2", which keeps the existing load semantics):

```lean
-- SHAPE ONLY — neither predicate is defined yet; see step 5a.
theorem parse_iff_grammar (input : String) :
    (∃ docs, parseYaml input = .ok docs)
      ↔ ExactSurfaceLanguage input ∧ SerializationWellFormed input
```

`ExactSurfaceLanguage` is `InYamlLanguage` with reasons 1's over-approximations
closed — the work rows 12 and 19 already describe, plus the audit's fifth and
sixth.  `SerializationWellFormed` is new and carries reason 2: anchor/alias
ordering and tag-handle declaration state, per document.  **Nothing defines it
yet, and nothing proves the shape above**; it is recorded as the target, not as
an achievement.  The alternative shape the audit offered — a syntax-only
capstone with the stateful conditions kept out of the statement entirely — was
not chosen, because it would stop advertising what `parseYaml` actually
enforces.
